questions.q: A 35-year-old man presents with a painless genital ulcer with indurated edges and a clean base. Gram stain shows no organisms but dark-field microscopy reveals spirochetes. Which is the drug of choice?
opts: Benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM single dose
questions.exp: Primary syphilis (chancre) caused by Treponema pallidum. Benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM single dose is the drug of choice for primary, secondary, and early latent syphilis.

questions.q: A 28-year-old farmer presents with multiple sinuses over the foot discharging white granules. Microscopy shows hyaline, septate hyphae. Which organism is most likely responsible?
questions.exp: White grain mycetoma is caused by Pseudallescheria boydii (eumycetoma). Black grain eumycetoma is caused by Madurella mycetomatis. Actinomyces causes actinomycetoma with white to yellowish grains.

questions.q: A 25-year-old presents with hypopigmented anaesthetic patches on the trunk and thickened greater auricular nerve. Slit skin smear is negative. Which type of leprosy is this?
questions.exp: Tuberculoid leprosy (TT) is characterized by well-defined hypopigmented anaesthetic patches (1-2 lesions), thickened peripheral nerves, and negative slit skin smear (paucibacillary). Treated with 6 months rifampicin + dapsone.

questions.q: A 45-year-old woman with butterfly rash, photosensitivity, and joint pain. ANA is positive (1:320). Which antibody is most specific for systemic lupus erythematosus?
questions.exp: Anti-Smith (Sm) antibodies are highly specific (99%) for SLE though not sensitive (25-30%). Anti-dsDNA is also fairly specific and correlates with disease activity. Anti-Ro and anti-La are associated with Sjogren syndrome and neonatal lupus.

questions.q: A 60-year-old presents with tense bullae on normal-appearing skin and mucous membrane involvement. Direct immunofluorescence shows linear IgG and C3 deposition at the basement membrane zone. Diagnosis?
questions.exp: Bullous pemphigoid shows tense bullae on erythematous or normal skin, minimal mucous membrane involvement, linear IgG/C3 at BMZ on DIF. Target antigen is BP180 (type XVII collagen) and BP230. Anti-desmoglein antibodies target pemphigus.

questions.q: A 50-year-old presents with scaly erythematous plaques over extensor surfaces with silvery scales, nail pitting, and Auspitz sign. Which cytokine plays the central role in pathogenesis?
questions.exp: IL-17 (specifically IL-17A produced by Th17 cells) is the central cytokine in psoriasis pathogenesis. This is the basis for IL-17 inhibitors (secukinumab, ixekizumab, bimekizumab) used in psoriasis treatment. IL-4 is key in atopic dermatitis.

questions.q: A 30-year-old with recurrent vesicles on the genitals. HSV-2 is confirmed. Which statement about HSV is FALSE?
opts: HSV-1 establishes latency in trigeminal ganglia
HSV-2 establishes latency in sacral ganglia
Acyclovir acts by inhibiting viral DNA polymerase after phosphorylation by viral thymidine kinase
questions.exp: Primary HSV-2 infection is frequently asymptomatic or subclinical (70-80% of cases). Most people with HSV-2 are unaware they are infected. Viral thymidine kinase phosphorylates acyclovir to monophosphate form, and cellular kinases convert it to triphosphate which inhibits viral DNA polymerase.

questions.q: A 40-year-old man presents with leonine facies, madarosis, and diffuse thickening of earlobes. Slit skin smear shows globi. Which reaction type is he most at risk for?
opts: Type 2 lepra reaction only in borderline leprosy
questions.exp: Lepromatous leprosy (LL) with globi on SSS is the type most at risk for Type 2 reaction (Erythema nodosum leprosum/ENL), an immune complex-mediated reaction. Type 1 reaction (reversal reaction) occurs in borderline leprosy. Lucio phenomenon occurs in diffuse lepromatous leprosy.

questions.q: A 22-year-old woman presents with multiple comedones, inflammatory papules and pustules on the face. Cystic acne is present. Which systemic treatment is indicated for severe nodulocystic acne?
questions.exp: Oral isotretinoin (0.5-1 mg/kg/day) for 4-6 months achieving cumulative dose of 120-150 mg/kg is the gold standard for severe nodulocystic acne. It acts on all four pathogenic factors: sebum production, follicular keratinization, C. acnes, and inflammation.

questions.q: A 55-year-old presents with a pearly, translucent papule with telangiectasias on the nasolabial fold. Biopsy shows palisading nuclei with peripheral retraction artifact. Diagnosis?
questions.exp: Basal cell carcinoma (BCC) is the most common skin cancer. Nodular BCC shows pearly papule with rolled borders, telangiectasias. Histology shows palisading of nuclei at periphery with retraction artifact (clefting). Most common site is nose, specifically nasolabial fold.

questions.q: A 70-year-old presents with hyperkeratotic warty lesion on the lip. Biopsy shows keratin pearls, individual cell keratinization, and intercellular bridges. Risk for metastasis in this site?
questions.exp: Squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) of the lip has a metastatic rate of 11-14%. SCCs arising on lip, ear, mucous membranes, or non-sun-exposed areas have higher metastatic potential than those on sun-exposed skin (metastatic rate <2%). Marjolin's ulcer has the highest rate (30%).

questions.q: A 35-year-old HIV-positive patient presents with multiple well-defined pink-violaceous plaques on the extremities. Biopsy shows proliferating spindle cells and vascular slits with extravasated RBCs. HHV-8 is detected. Treatment of choice?
questions.exp: AIDS-related Kaposi sarcoma (epidemic KS) - primary treatment is HAART which restores immune function. HAART alone can lead to regression. Liposomal doxorubicin or paclitaxel is used for widespread/visceral disease. HHV-8 is the causative virus.

questions.q: A 28-year-old presents with diffuse hair loss after delivery 3 months ago. Trichogram shows predominance of telogen hairs. Diagnosis and expected outcome?
opts: Alopecia areata - requires treatment with corticosteroids
Telogen effluvium - self-limiting, resolves within 6-12 months
questions.exp: Postpartum telogen effluvium occurs 2-4 months after delivery due to transition of anagen hairs to telogen phase induced by hormonal changes. It is self-limiting and resolves within 6-12 months as hair cycle normalizes. Trichogram shows >25% telogen hairs.

questions.q: A 45-year-old presents with generalized hyperpigmentation, especially in sun-exposed areas, palmar creases, and buccal mucosa. Serum cortisol is low. Diagnosis?
questions.exp: Addison's disease (primary adrenal insufficiency) causes generalized hyperpigmentation due to elevated ACTH and MSH (melanocyte-stimulating hormone). Characteristic sites are sun-exposed areas, palmar creases, pressure points, buccal mucosa, and scars.

questions.q: A 20-year-old presents with white patches on the skin with complete loss of melanocytes. Wood's lamp examination enhances the lesions. Which investigation confirms the diagnosis?
opts: Skin biopsy showing absent melanocytes with Masson-Fontana stain
questions.exp: Vitiligo is confirmed by skin biopsy showing complete absence of melanocytes (Masson-Fontana stain). Wood's lamp (Wood's light) enhances vitiligo patches as brilliant white fluorescence due to complete absence of melanin. ANA may be positive in autoimmune vitiligo.

questions.q: A 55-year-old presents with pruritic, violaceous, polygonal, flat-topped papules with Wickham's striae on the wrist and oral mucosal white lacy pattern. Diagnosis and characteristic histological feature?
opts: Lichen planus - saw-tooth rete ridges and band-like lymphocytic infiltrate
questions.exp: Lichen planus presents with the 4 P's: purple, polygonal, pruritic, papules. Wickham's striae are pathognomonic. Histology shows: saw-tooth rete ridges, band-like lymphocytic infiltrate at DEJ, colloid (Civatte) bodies, and hypergranulosis. Oral involvement with Wickham's striae is characteristic.

questions.q: A 32-year-old man presents with a painless grouped vesicles on erythematous base in the genital area. Tzanck smear shows multinucleated giant cells. PCR confirms HSV-2. Which antiviral is appropriate for episodic therapy?
opts: Acyclovir 200mg five times daily for 5 days
All of the above are appropriate options
questions.exp: All three antivirals are FDA-approved for episodic treatment of recurrent genital herpes. Valacyclovir (prodrug of acyclovir with better bioavailability) 500mg BD for 3 days, Famciclovir 125mg BD for 5 days, and Acyclovir 200mg 5x/day for 5 days are all acceptable. Suppressive therapy reduces recurrences by 70-80%.

questions.q: A 42-year-old woman presents with bilateral facial hyperpigmentation sparing the perioral area, worsening in summer. She is on oral contraceptives. Dermoscopy shows brownish pigmentation in the epidermis. Treatment?
opts: Triple combination cream (HQ + tretinoin + steroid) with strict sun protection
questions.exp: Melasma management involves strict photoprotection as the cornerstone. Triple combination cream (hydroquinone 4% + tretinoin 0.05% + fluocinolone acetonide 0.01%) - Kligman's modified formula - is the most effective topical treatment. OCPs worsen melasma and should be discontinued if possible.

questions.q: A 65-year-old immunocompromised patient presents with painful grouped vesicles along a dermatomal distribution on the left thorax. Which complication causes the greatest concern?
questions.exp: Postherpetic neuralgia (PHN) - persistent pain >3 months after healing of zoster - is the most significant complication, occurring in 10-15% of cases (increases with age). Early antiviral treatment reduces PHN risk. Zoster vaccine (Shingrix) is recommended for adults >=50 years.

questions.q: A 25-year-old presents with tinea versicolor (pityriasis versicolor). KOH mount shows 'spaghetti and meatballs' appearance. Which oral antifungal is FDA approved specifically for this condition?
questions.exp: Ketoconazole 400mg single dose (with sweating induced after 12 hours without washing) is the recommended oral treatment for pityriasis versicolor. It has efficacy against Malassezia species. Terbinafine is NOT effective against Malassezia (no ergosterol pathway in this organism for terbinafine to target).

questions.q: A 50-year-old diabetic patient presents with a tender erythematous plaque with sharp margins on the leg, fever, and leukocytosis. Which organism is most commonly responsible?
questions.exp: Erysipelas is a superficial form of cellulitis with well-demarcated borders caused predominantly by Group A Streptococcus (S. pyogenes). It involves the upper dermis and superficial lymphatics. Cellulitis has indistinct borders and is caused by both Streptococcus and Staphylococcus. Treatment: penicillin/amoxicillin.

questions.q: A 40-year-old presents with targetoid skin lesions with central blistering, mucosal involvement (eyes, mouth, genitalia), and systemic symptoms after starting trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole. The diagnosis is?
opts: Drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS)
questions.exp: Stevens-Johnson syndrome (SJS) = erythema multiforme major: <10% BSA detachment, mucosal involvement of >=2 sites, targetoid lesions. TEN involves >30% BSA. Common culprits: sulfonamides, anticonvulsants, allopurinol, NSAIDs. Pathogenesis involves drug-specific cytotoxic T cells and granulysin.

questions.q: A 60-year-old woman presents with tense blisters and milia on sun-exposed dorsal hands. Plasma porphyrins are elevated. Urine shows pink fluorescence under Wood's lamp. Diagnosis?
questions.exp: Porphyria cutanea tarda (PCT): photosensitive bullae and milia on dorsal hands, elevated uroporphyrins in urine (pink-red fluorescence on Wood's lamp), hyperpigmentation, hypertrichosis. Caused by uroporphyrinogen decarboxylase deficiency. Associated with alcohol, hepatitis C, iron overload, estrogen.

questions.q: A 30-year-old man with multiple partners presents with a painless ulcer followed by inguinal lymphadenopathy with a groove sign (groove of Poupart's ligament). Diagnosis?
questions.exp: Lymphogranuloma venereum (LGV): painless transient ulcer (stage 1), then inguinal lymphadenopathy with GROOVE SIGN (pathognomonic - lymph nodes above and below inguinal ligament separated by groove). Caused by Chlamydia trachomatis serovars L1, L2, L3. Treatment: doxycycline 100mg BD for 21 days.

questions.q: A 38-year-old atopic woman presents with intensely pruritic excoriated papules and lichenified plaques in the antecubital fossa, back of knees, and neck. Serum IgE is markedly elevated. Which finding on patch test is expected?
opts: Positive patch test to nickel sulfate
Positive patch test to fragrance mix
Usually no relevant allergens on patch test
questions.exp: Atopic dermatitis (AD) is an IgE-mediated type I hypersensitivity disorder. Patch testing evaluates type IV (delayed) hypersensitivity/contact allergy. Most AD patients do not have relevant positive patch tests. The disease is driven by Th2 cytokines (IL-4, IL-13) and IgE elevation, not contact allergy.

questions.q: A patient undergoes dermoscopy for a pigmented lesion. Features include atypical pigment network, irregular streaks, regression structures (white scar-like areas and blue-gray peppering), and multiple colors. These features are most consistent with?
questions.exp: Dermoscopic criteria for melanoma: atypical pigment network, irregular streaks/pseudopods, regression structures (white scar-like areas + blue-gray peppering), blue-white veil, multiple colors (>=5-6 colors). ABCD rule (Asymmetry, Border, Color, Diameter). Menzies method and 7-point checklist are other scoring systems.

questions.q: A 25-year-old presents with scarring alopecia - follicular plugging, erythema, and scaling within patches on the scalp. Skin biopsy shows periadnexal lymphocytic infiltrate, interfollicular mucin deposition, and follicular plugging. Diagnosis?
questions.exp: Discoid lupus erythematosus: scarring alopecia with follicular plugging, erythema, hypopigmented atrophic center with hyperpigmented border. Histology: periadnexal lymphocytic infiltrate, mucin in dermis, thickened BMZ, follicular plugging. DIF shows lupus band (IgG, C3 at DEJ). Treatment: hydroxychloroquine.

questions.q: A 45-year-old diabetic undergoes a chemical peel for acne scars. Post-procedure, he develops persistent erythema, mottled hyperpigmentation, and textural changes 6 weeks later. This complication is best described as?
opts: Chemical peel depth exceeded target and caused scarring
questions.exp: Persistent erythema beyond 4 weeks, textural changes, and mottled pigmentation after chemical peel indicate that the peel went deeper than intended, causing dermal injury and scarring. Risk factors include darker skin type, recent isotretinoin use, diabetes, and application over bony prominences. Prophylactic antivirals prevent HSV reactivation.

questions.q: A 55-year-old man presents with firm, hyperpigmented plaques over the trunk with orange-peel texture. He has bilateral ptosis and proximal muscle weakness. Skin biopsy shows mucin deposition in the dermis. The likely diagnosis is?
questions.exp: Scleromyxedema: generalized papular mucinosis with systemic involvement. Features: firm papules/plaques, skin induration (Shar-Pei sign), periorbital involvement with leonine facies, and associated systemic features including myopathy, cardiomyopathy, neurological symptoms. Associated with IgG lambda paraproteinemia. Histology: fibroblast proliferation + mucin.

questions.q: A 55-year-old woman presents with multiple itchy papules and wheals with a central punctum after a bee sting. She has a history of similar reactions. Which is the most appropriate immediate treatment if anaphylaxis develops?
questions.exp: Epinephrine (adrenaline) 1:1000 solution 0.3-0.5mL SC/IM (preferably anterolateral thigh) is the drug of choice for anaphylaxis. It acts on alpha-1 (vasoconstriction), beta-1 (increased HR, contractility), and beta-2 (bronchodilation) receptors. Antihistamines and steroids are adjuncts, not first-line treatment.

questions.q: Which layer of the epidermis contains the mitotically active basal cells that give rise to all epidermal keratinocytes?
questions.exp: Stratum basale (germinativum) is the deepest epidermal layer containing proliferative keratinocytes, melanocytes, and Merkel cells. Keratinocytes undergo terminal differentiation progressing from basale to spinosum (desmosomes/prickle cells) to granulosum (keratohyalin granules, lamellar bodies) to corneum (corneocytes). Transit time: 28-56 days.
